purpose: Single source of truth for tick-accurate runtime work: ASM references, Python entrypoints, current confidence, blind spots, and regression tests.

status_legend.asm_verified: The runtime behavior is intentionally matched to a concrete ASM branch/address and covered by enough checks for current use.
status_legend.asm_partial: The runtime behavior has ASM evidence, but timing, edge cases, or state transitions are still incomplete.
status_legend.data_verified: Data/asset mapping is confirmed, but runtime behavior is not fully traced.
status_legend.heuristic: Implemented from observation or inference, not yet backed by concrete ASM.
status_legend.known_wrong: A mismatch against the original is known and documented.

phases.title: Mission fixed DOS tick ordering
exact_claims: One DOS tick snapshots dynamic render positions before simulation mutation.
When DS:69F5/DS:69F6 death state is active, the death branch runs before actor updates instead of freezing actors.
The moving-platform carry branch can still catch the death sprite after the death arc mutates Y on the same tick.
blind_spots: The full mission loop around 0x1B5D is not yet represented as a named phase table.
The restart helper at 0x520:0x011A is still only partially understood, so tick-order after death expiration is approximate.
Some interaction dispatch inside update_player_interactions is still broad and should be split into exact subphases.
next_actions: Trace the post-0x1B5D actor/update call chain into a named tick phase map.
Split update_player_interactions into ordered ASM-backed subdispatchers.
Trace 0x520:0x011A persistence/game-over behavior.

phases.title: Hard-death bounce arc and clamp
exact_claims: DS:69F6 starts at 0x23 and indexes a signed word table.
The table value is subtracted from player Y, so positive values move up and negative values move down.
Y clamps between 0x10 and DS:683A + 0xB8 without normal collision.
blind_spots: Exact two-cel death draw timing still needs frame-by-frame DOSBox validation.
The lives-zero game-over/menu branch is still approximated.
Exact score/ammo/inventory persistence through the restart helper is not fully traced.
next_actions: Extract the death signed-step table into a documented exe_* module with the ASM table offset.
Trace 0x520:0x011A and update reset/persistence semantics.
Capture DOSBox reference frames for death sprite/camera clamp timing.

phases.title: Normal mission horizontal, jump, and fall motion
asm_refs: SAM1:0x801F DS:6EC1 normal-jump guard inside platform carry
exact_claims: Horizontal movement uses the EXE-style step ramp and atomic destination probes for normal map collision.
Normal falling/jumping uses the unshifted 34EA/34AF table: counter 1 reads byte 0x34B0=0, counter 2 reads 8, and B8B3 static landing probes perform the snap/clamp paths.
The upward jump probe is separate from the downward fall probe.

BC0E fall/jump Y updates are applied before the later horizontal B7D9 destination probe in the runtime tick, so a same-tick jump ascent or landing snap can align the player with a one-tile passage before horizontal acceptance.
The corrected table creates the original modulo-16 jump/fall alignment frames, including the falling sequence from +8 mod 16 back to tile-aligned after 1,1,2,2,2 px.
Moving-platform carry/catch honors the ASM DS:6EC1 guard: active normal jump skips player snap/carry/fall-counter reset, while hard-death DS:69F5 still does not block platform catch.
blind_spots: The exact caller/wrapper that sequences BAF5-style horizontal control and BC0E vertical control still needs a full overlay trace; pass 130/131 cover the observed one-tile opening regression with an ASM-anchored ordering reconstruction and corrected table indexing.
The raw 0x62 dynamic actor/player overlap branch is not fully isolated.
Actor-backed solid fall overlap remains a reconstruction around exact static probes.
Ladder/direct vertical flags DS:6EC3/DS:6EC4 are not implemented.
Difficulty modifiers DS:69B0/DS:69A4 are not modeled.
The complete raw 0x62 actor branch, including DS:6EC2 side effects, camera carry, and jump-off-platform DOSBox timing, still needs a full trace; pass 133 only fixes the decoded DS:6EC1 skip gate.
next_actions: Trace the 0x520:0x68F5 / 0x520:0x6A0E player-control wrappers to turn the pass-130 ordering reconstruction into a fully named ASM phase.
Add deterministic motion probes for wall approach, ceiling hit, edge fall, and landing.
Trace DS:6EC3/DS:6EC4 ladder/direct vertical movement.
Isolate raw 0x62 actor/player branch and compare against current crossing reconstruction.
Verify the corrected DS:34AF indexing against more DOSBox jump/fall captures near one-tile openings and ceilings.
Trace raw 0x62 platform branch 0x7FA6..0x8165 with live DOS captures for jumping from a moving platform and compare DS:6EC1/DS:6EC2 transitions.

phases.title: Raw 0xA7 pushable barrel actor interaction
asm_refs: SAM1:0x532D player movement is not barrel movement
DS:34AF player vertical table is not used for raw 0xA7 fall
exact_claims: Raw 0xA7 enters a special actor-family branch instead of behaving like a plain static solid tile.
SAM1:0x83C4..0x848A tests player/barrel contact with shrunken X intervals x+3..x+12 for both rectangles and full Y intervals y..y+15.
The runtime uses that ASM rectangle for player/barrel actor overlap, dynamic barrel body collision, and barrel top-contact horizontal eligibility.
The reconstructed vertical fall path keeps X fixed and only uses landing/foot probes; it does not use broad side-body collision to stop falling.
Horizontal barrel pushes still use broad barrel-vs-world collision for the barrel body itself.
A successful horizontal push that leaves the barrel without floor support marks it unsupported before the next fall tick.
SAM1:0x848A..0x84E9 is a destructive/score rewrite path: visible object 0x00AA, state 0x1389, DS:34DA=0x10, score +0x03E8, sound 0x04. It must not be used as the wall-blocked push behavior.

State 0x1389 moves actor Y upward by 2 pixels per actor tick with a clamp at absolute 0x10, decrements the 0x10 timer, and removes the actor when the timer expires; this remains represented only for destructive/score transient states, not normal wall pushing.

A wall-blocked push preserves raw object 0xA7/state 0x1388, gives the barrel body-pass-through/top-solid semantics, flips the barrel direction away from the wall, and restores it on the free side after the player crosses the ASM shrunken leading edge.

Wall-release free-side restoration no longer waits for a live front-wall body probe; pass 125 uses the SAM1:0x83C4..0x842F shrunken x+3..x+12 leading-edge crossing and restores the barrel just outside that same shrunken interval (~10/11px clearance).

During an active wall-release window, normal horizontal movement routes through the per-pixel path until the release is restored; otherwise pass-through barrels are skipped by player_touching_barrel() and the free-side restoration is never polled.
Ordinary raw-0xA7 push uses a named 4px actor-step reconstruction instead of the player current 1/2/4px substep.
Unsupported raw-0xA7 fall no longer indexes the player DS:34AF vertical table; it attempts BARREL_ACTOR_STEP_PX pixels and still resolves landing one pixel at a time.

A pushed-off-edge raw 0xA7 enters a falling-locked vertical actor phase in the Python reconstruction: side contact no longer invokes try_push_barrel(), so the barrel keeps its X column until landing clears the lock.
blind_spots: The exact ASM caller/store for the wall-blocked push restoration is still not isolated; current code is a reconstruction from DOS observation plus the ASM shrunken x+3..x+12 contact rectangle and the negative proof that 0x848A is the wrong destructive branch. Pass 125 corrects pass 124 by removing the too-late live front-wall gate, and pass 126 fixes the Python polling path so the active release can actually restore after becoming pass-through; it still needs DOSBox pixel capture for exact tick/candidate rounding.
The 0x1389 redraw cleanup calls are documented but not reproduced at the individual dirty-tile call level.
Helper 0x547C projectile-hit branch at SAM1:0x82F2..0x8335 is traced as a projectile overlap helper, but barrel shot/destruction gameplay is still not implemented as its own path.
No DOSBox reference capture yet for pushing while partially overlapping another dynamic actor.

Pushed-off-edge fall timing remains partial; pass 127 removes the unsupported player-gravity-table coupling and uses a named 4px actor-step reconstruction, and pass 128 locks unsupported fall against further side pushes, but the exact 0x1388 store/tick that starts falling still needs ASM/DOSBox confirmation.
next_actions: Find the actual wall-blocked push/restoration caller/store in ASM and compare pass-125/pass-126 shrunken-edge restoration and polling against DOSBox; do not reuse the 0x848A score rewrite for this case.
Trace or implement the helper-0x547C projectile-hit path for raw 0xA7 separately from player-contact release.
Create a tiny DOSBox reference setup for blocked pushes, pushed-off-ledge timing, and barrel/player partial overlap.
Trace the exact post-push unsupported 0x1388 transition/store and compare the pass-127 4px actor-step plus pass-128 falling-lock behavior against a DOSBox reference capture.
Decide whether the individual 0x1389 redraw calls matter in the Python renderer or can remain a documented no-op.

phases.title: Level-0 overworld movement, collision, camera, and entrance tick

Movement checks the attempted offset before writing player position.
Collision samples the +0x1CC body byte at player-origin rectangle x+3/x+12 and y/y+15, ignoring +0x1CD.
Camera registers DS:6838/DS:683A use fixed margins rather than a centered camera helper.
blind_spots: Entrance-to-level mapping is still row-major prototype behavior.
Persistent completion/progression flags are not fully traced.
Original popup/table windows are not implemented.
Remaining choke points need coordinate-specific DOSBox comparisons.
next_actions: Trace entrance marker dispatch and completion flag writes.
Implement original table/popup renderer before replacing prototype labels.
Add coordinate-specific overworld movement reference tests.

phases.title: Animated decor and decorative/non-contact policy
exact_claims: Raw 0x40 / object 0x0131 / state 0x2B advances animation counters and does not call the player-contact helper 0x53C4.
The lower cel of raw 0x40 is bank9:1 in the current model.
State 0x2C routes contact through an explicit object-0x0103 helper call.
blind_spots: Frame sources should be generated from renderer/object ranges instead of hand-coded refs.
The full raw 0x78 frame-source family still needs a focused renderer-table audit.
Decor/hazard naming should be split so non-contact animated tiles do not inherit hazard assumptions.
next_actions: Annotate state 0x2B/0x2C ASM branches next to renderer frame sources.
Generate frame-source tables from the original renderer data.
Add regression fixtures for raw 0x40 and raw 0x78 contact expectations.

phases.title: Projectile, enemy contact, and hit policy tick
exact_claims: Ceiling laser state 0x21 has a strict player-origin x gate and uses actor_y+8 for spawned laser origin.
0x00C7 is rewritten to object 0x72/state 0x89 for ceiling beams.
Object 0x72 state 0x25 and state 0x89 have separated damage outcomes in the current runtime.
Stationary launcher states 0x0A/0x0B keep DS:34DA as an elapsed timer that increments before row/facing gates and resets only after a successful helper-0x5784 spawn.
Raw 0x52/state 0x0A fires object 0x01D6 at actor_x+8, actor_y, direction +1, speed 4 when actor_x < player_x and the row gate matches.
Raw 0x51/state 0x0B fires object 0x01D6 at actor_x-8, actor_y, direction -1, speed 4 when actor_x > player_x and the row gate matches.
Raw 0x51/0x52 actor bodies are not solid player blockers and do not hurt on body contact; their threat is projectile 0x01D6.
Stationary launcher helper 0x5784 receives actor_y; Python stores projectile.y = actor_y+7 only to compensate horizontal-projectile rendering at y-7.
Raw 0x51/0x52 stationary launchers are excluded from the generic body-touch fallback; only their emitted 0x01D6 projectile is hostile.
Raw 0x3C/state 0x0C fires rocket object 0x01E8 at actor_x+16, actor_y, direction +1, speed 4 when actor_x < player_x and the row gate matches.
Raw 0x3D/state 0x0D fires rocket object 0x01EC at actor_x-16, actor_y, direction -1, speed 4 when actor_x > player_x and the row gate matches.
Helper 0x5784 maps object 0x01D6 to projectile state 0x07 and rocket objects 0x01E8/0x01EC to projectile state 0x0E.
Projectile states 0x07 and 0x0E call helper 0x53C4 for player contact; this hurts the player but does not consume or rewrite the projectile slot.
Helper 0x547C, not player contact, owns stationary shot/rocket impact consumption.
Python compensates stationary horizontal projectile rendering with y=actor_y+7 and hit_y_offset=-7 so the 0x53C4 damage rectangle remains anchored at the ASM actor_y.
Raw 0x3C/0x3D rocket projectiles animate with decoded bank4 frames 37..39 when moving right and 41..43 when moving left.
Raw 0x75/state 0x23 initializes object 0x006D with DS:34E6=0, DS:34E2=+1, DS:34DC=3, and does not patrol as a normal walker.
State 0x23 calls helper 0x53C4 for player contact damage; player contact does not decrement the three-hit counter or trigger the score/shrapnel path.
State 0x23 decrements DS:34DC only when helper 0x547C reports projectile/actor impact; after the third hit it awards 1000 and enters the object 0x00AA/state 0x1389 follow-up.
Raw 0x75 rendering uses bank2 tiles 8..11 from frame counter 1..19 and must not accidentally enter the generic left-facing 12..15 family.
blind_spots: The full projectile object/state table is incomplete.
Impact spark versus silent projectile consumption is only partially separated; helper 0x547C still needs exact side-effect tracing.
Object-0x72 foreground redraw and map-collision side effects are approximate.
Raw 0x3C/0x3D launcher projectile path is now traced, but exact body-contact dispatcher absence for the launcher bodies still needs a separate audit.
The generic enemy-body contact fallback is still exclusion-based; it needs a full ASM-derived allowlist so new actor kinds do not inherit damage accidentally.
Raw 0x75 object 0x00AA/state 0x1389 follow-up draw/clear is still approximated after the hit counter expires.
Rocket animation frames are data-backed from decoded bank4; exact state-0x0E draw pointer math should still be traced if visual offsets differ.
next_actions: Build a complete projectile object/state table from ASM helper 0x5784 and dispatcher branches.
Trace helper 0x547C for stationary shot/rocket solid impact and visible impact sprites.
Add broader projectile-policy regression coverage beyond stationary launchers.
Trace object-0x72 map-collision foreground redraw side effects.
Audit check_enemy_touch() against the ASM contact dispatcher and turn the temporary exclusion list into a verified allowlist.
Trace raw 0x75 object 0x00AA/state 0x1389 follow-up draw/clear sequence after the third 0x547C hit.
Trace state-0x0E rocket draw pointer math if the bank4 animation looks offset in DOSBox.
